md-baltimore-county-2026-sa-david-sarah.name: Sarah R. David
md-baltimore-county-2026-sa-david-sarah.bio: Career prosecutor who manages a team prosecuting public corruption across Maryland; former Baltimore City prosecutor and chief of staff to the Senate Judicial Proceedings Committee chairman.

positions.stance: Will collect and share crime data, use vertical prosecution for complex cases, and add a Diversion Coordinator so prosecutors focus on violent, repeat offenders.
Will prosecute sexual assault and domestic violence cases "with vigor," track and report each case's progress, and prevent assaults through education in schools.
Supports rehabilitation with accountability, publishing juvenile crime trend data, and creating a specialized Juvenile Division.
Will partner with schools, law enforcement and community groups to prevent violence in schools and address online bullying and harassment.
Supports a robust Victim/Witness Services Program, expanded community outreach, and public-private partnerships for crime prevention.

md-baltimore-county-2026-register-burrel.name: Alexis Burrell-Rohde
md-baltimore-county-2026-register-burrel.bio: Baltimore County Register of Wills; former estates and trusts attorney and assistant attorney general representing Maryland's Registers of Wills and Orphans' Courts.

md-baltimore-county-2026-sheriff-boatwri.name: Clyde E. Boatwright
md-baltimore-county-2026-sheriff-boatwri.bio: Police officer for 25 years and graduate of Northwestern University's School of Police Staff and Command.

positions.stance: Calls domestic violence the campaign's "top priority" and proposes a 24-hour Domestic Violence Unit to quickly serve court orders and respond to emergencies.
Will collaborate with external partners to increase the presence of deputy sheriffs in communities across the county.
Will upgrade technology and adopt "21st-century policing best practices" for a more efficient workforce.

md-baltimore-county-2026-sheriff-burke-m.name: Michael F. Burke
md-baltimore-county-2026-sheriff-burke-m.bio: Law enforcement professional and military veteran with more than 25 years in military police, counterintelligence, investigations and emergency services.

positions.stance: Supports aggressive warrant service, coordinated multi-agency operations and targeting repeat offenders, blending intelligence-driven enforcement with community-based prevention.
Will prioritize recruitment, retention and training to rebuild a fully staffed Sheriff's Office and restore deputy morale.
Will ensure secure, efficient, transparent courthouse and transport operations using modern technology and improved coordination with corrections.
Commits to being a Sheriff "present in the community—not behind a desk," meeting regularly with residents, businesses and civic groups.
Will work with county, state and federal partners to disrupt trafficking while supporting addiction and recovery programs.

md-prince-georges-2026-exec-braveboy-ais.name: Aisha Braveboy
md-prince-georges-2026-exec-braveboy-ais.bio: Prince George's County Executive; former two-term Prince George's County State's Attorney.

positions.stance: Lists getting the county's "fiscal house in order" as a priority, citing elimination of a $170 million structural deficit without raising taxes.
Prioritizes clean communities through stronger 311 responses, cleaned lots, and cleared litter and debris.
Prioritizes reducing crime and cites supporting the largest police recruitment class in over a decade.
Prioritizes student success, citing teacher vacancy reduction and increased investment in special education, reading and math programs.
Supports giving seniors a direct voice through cabinet-level positions and has proposed a county-wide senior utility assistance program.

md-prince-georges-2026-council-atlarge-h.name: Sydney Harrison
md-prince-georges-2026-council-atlarge-h.bio: Prince George's County Council member for District 9 since 2018 and two-time council vice-chair; former Clerk of the Circuit Court and plumbing company founder.

positions.stance: Champions increased public-school funding, workforce training, and youth enrichment.
Committed to helping seniors "experience a higher level of care and standard of living."
"Fully supports continued investment in police, fire/EMS, and community partnership."
Supports fiscally responsible leadership as the county works to regain its Triple-A bond rating.
Calls creating Plan 2050 critical, aligning land use, transportation, housing, economic development, and environmental goals.

md-prince-georges-2026-council-atlarge-i.name: Jolene Ivey
md-prince-georges-2026-council-atlarge-i.bio: Chair of the Prince George's County Council; former State Delegate and chair of the Prince George's County House Delegation.

md-prince-georges-2026-sa-jackson-tara.name: Tara Jackson
md-prince-georges-2026-sa-jackson-tara.bio: Prince George's County State's Attorney; former Acting County Executive, Chief Administrative Officer and Deputy County Attorney.

positions.stance: Says the State's Attorney should "be tough on repeat and violent offenders."
Says the office should "protect residents from financial fraud and abuse" and pursue justice for every victim.
Supports holding young people accountable for bad choices "while creating pathways for redemption and restoration."
Will lead an office that is "responsive, transparent, and accountable" and not used "for politics or power."
Will treat crime victims "with empathy and respect" and ensure persons charged with crimes receive due process.

md-prince-georges-2026-register-route-jo.name: Jocelyn Route
md-prince-georges-2026-register-route-jo.bio: Social worker and Senior Advisor – Wellness Integrator at M-NCPPC's Department of Parks and Recreation; former SAMHSA public health advisor and Board of Education member.

md-prince-georges-2026-sheriff-carr-john.name: John D. B. Carr
md-prince-georges-2026-sheriff-carr-john.bio: Sheriff of Prince George's County since December 2022.

positions.stance: Will partner with community organizations on resource awareness and create programs engaging youth and protecting vulnerable adults.
Proposes a dedicated warrant task force focused on reducing gun violence, prioritizing warrants involving firearms and violent offenders.
Will strengthen and expand domestic violence programs and resources so survivors and families have needed support.
Supports new agency, court and hospital collaborations and a dedicated county facility for adolescents with mental health challenges.

mo-stcharles-2026-executive-ehlmann-stev.name: Steve Ehlmann
mo-stcharles-2026-executive-ehlmann-stev.bio: St. Charles County Executive since 2006; former State Representative, State Senator, Circuit Judge and county Director of Administration.

positions.stance: Will continue working with police and prosecutors "to maintain a low crime rate and keep our families safe."
Believes economic development resources should attract quality jobs that help the region grow, not move big box retail between cities.
Will keep "fighting to keep government small and efficient so residents can keep more of their hard earned money."
Prioritizes modern road infrastructure and smart traffic technology, citing major road projects and the Gateway Green Light program.
Supports growing parks and trails, preserving historic sites, and county-wide public health efforts including fighting the opioid crisis.

mo-stcharles-2026-executive-veneziano-da.name: David Veneziano
mo-stcharles-2026-executive-veneziano-da.bio: Biotechnology professional with a physics degree from Clark University and an MBA from the University of South Carolina.

positions.stance: Supports renter protections, inclusionary zoning for affordable housing, and targeted financial relief for working-class families and seniors.
Would ensure studies are performed "to justify a ban on large scale data centers" to protect water, electricity and environment.
Says term limits are needed for the County Executive and campaign finance changes are needed to limit large donations.
Opposes the county's 287(g) partnership with ICE, saying it "has no place in St Charles County."
Supports taking down privately owned Flock cameras and establishing strict rules protecting data gathered on residents.

mo-stcharles-2026-director-elections-bah.name: Kurt Bahr
mo-stcharles-2026-director-elections-bah.bio: St. Charles County Director of Elections since 2018; former Missouri State Representative for District 102 and U.S. Air Force finance officer.

positions.stance: Commits to "every ballot counted exactly as cast — verified through bipartisan procedures and independent audits."
Supports "certified equipment, strict chain of custody, and bipartisan oversight from start to finish."
Supports "transparent processes, open observation, and clear public reporting at every stage of every election."
Supports counting voter-marked paper ballots with certified tabulators, citing speed, accuracy, cost savings, and paper ballots retained for audits.

mo-stcharles-2026-collector-mcbride-mich.name: Michelle D McBride
mo-stcharles-2026-collector-mcbride-mich.bio: St. Charles County Collector of Revenue since 2007; former Fiscal Manager in the Collector's Office.

wi-waukesha-2026-sheriff-ollinger-nick.name: Nick Ollinger
wi-waukesha-2026-sheriff-ollinger-nick.bio: Commander of the Waukesha County Sheriff's Office Detective Bureau with more than 13 years in law enforcement.

co-adams-2026-clerk-zygielbaum-josh.name: Josh Zygielbaum
co-adams-2026-clerk-zygielbaum-josh.bio: Adams County Clerk and Recorder; former Thornton City Council member and U.S. Marine Corps sergeant who worked in community banking and finance.

positions.stance: Will continue improving services by "further developing friendlier tools and effectively staffing our offices to serve the public."
Will "continue to make strides in voter access," building on added drop boxes and Voter Service and Polling Centers.
Commits to continuing efforts "to ensure transparency and security" in the Clerk and Recorder's office.

co-adams-2026-clerk-hoopes-karen.name: Karen Hoopes
co-adams-2026-clerk-hoopes-karen.bio: Private- and public-sector manager with a master's degree in business management focused on organizational development.

positions.stance: Promises "clear processes, timely information, and easy-to-find resources" so voters know what to expect.
Promises "shorter lines, clearer instructions, and respectful help at every counter and online."
Supports strong safeguards and consistent procedures to protect sensitive information while keeping records accessible.
Supports practical technology upgrades that reduce errors and improve service "without wasting taxpayer dollars."

co-adams-2026-treasurer-anaya-ledeboer-j.name: Jason Anaya-Ledeboer
co-adams-2026-treasurer-anaya-ledeboer-j.bio: Finance professional with more than 25 years in banking who currently works at a Colorado credit union.

positions.stance: Will ensure every public dollar is collected, managed and distributed "with accuracy, accountability, and transparency."
Will focus on "stable, low-risk investment practices" that safeguard public funds and support long-term financial stability.
Will "bring integrity and transparency back to the office" so residents know their money is handled properly.
Will lead financial literacy efforts and partner with schools and community organizations on outreach.

co-adams-2026-assessor-swingle-thomas.name: Thomas Swingle
co-adams-2026-assessor-swingle-thomas.bio: Adams County Assessor and Colorado-licensed appraiser with over 24 years in the Assessor's Office, including roles as GIS specialist, appraiser and deputy assessor.

positions.stance: Will continue "modernizing systems to improve accuracy, fairness, and service" in property assessment.
Will make the assessment process more understandable and the office more responsive "through clear communication and accessible tools."

co-adams-2026-sheriff-goodell-mark.name: Mark Goodell
co-adams-2026-sheriff-goodell-mark.bio: Law enforcement officer for more than three decades, currently a deputy chief with a Colorado community.

positions.stance: Will work to reduce violent and property crime with data-driven policing strategies and ensure deputies have needed training and resources.
Will expand community outreach, hold regular town halls across the county, and give every neighborhood a voice in public safety decisions.
Will implement "clear policies, and regular public reporting, because accountability builds trust."
Will expand co-responder programs with trained professionals and strengthen detention-based mental health services.

co-adams-2026-sheriff-claps-gene.name: Gene R. Claps
co-adams-2026-sheriff-claps-gene.bio: Adams County Sheriff since January 2023 with more than 25 years at the Adams County Sheriff's Office.

positions.stance: Committed to rebuilding partnerships with local mental health providers and working toward an Adams County mental health detox center.
Will work with commissioners on whether a remodel, expansion or new jail is best, with any outcome requiring voter support.
Will keep fighting recidivism through pre-release programming, re-entry services, education and addiction treatment inside and after custody.
Committed to "developing evidence-based policing strategies" built on trust, ethics and transparency.

co-arapahoe-2026-clerk-lopez-joan.name: Joan Lopez
co-arapahoe-2026-clerk-lopez-joan.bio: Arapahoe County Clerk and Recorder since 2018, with 25 years working in the Arapahoe County clerk's office.

positions.stance: "Believes in a woman's right to choose."
Believes "in equal pay for equal work and LGBTQ rights."
Wants "immigration laws that strive for inclusion."
Believes "common sense gun laws will make our streets, schools and lives safer."
Wants justice system reforms that include drug addiction and mental health therapy rather than jail time.

co-arapahoe-2026-clerk-budd-annette.name: Annette Budd
co-arapahoe-2026-clerk-budd-annette.bio: Co-owner of a small, family-owned business that has served the Denver metro area for almost thirty years.

positions.stance: Supports walk-in appointments, promptly answered phone calls, and a user-friendly online appointment system at the Clerk's Office.
Supports ensuring "only eligible voters can register" and voter rolls "that are accurate and kept up to date."
Supports "Voter Identification presented before ballots are cast."
Supports "one day, in-person voting" with mail-in exceptions for military, sickness and travel.
Supports a "transparent voting system that is fully auditable with no connection to a computer or the internet."
